paragraphs.title: The Return of the Lord’s Glory to the Temple

easy.explanation: Ezekiel was brought to the gate that looked toward the east.
easy.q: To which gate was Ezekiel brought?

easy.explanation: The KJV says that the glory came from the way of the east.
easy.q: From which direction did the glory of the God of Israel come?

easy.explanation: The glory of the Lord came into the house through the eastern gate.
easy.q: Where did the glory of the Lord enter?

medium.explanation: The passage says, “and I fell upon my face.”
medium.q: What did Ezekiel do when he saw the vision of the glory?

answers: It could be heard only inside the house
medium.explanation: The comparison to many waters emphasizes the strength and majesty of the voice.
medium.q: What does the comparison to “a noise of many waters” suggest about the Lord’s voice?

answers: The earth was covered in darkness
The house disappeared from the earth
The glory of the Lord gave light across the earth
medium.explanation: The verse presents the Lord’s glory as shining over the earth.
medium.q: What is meant by “the earth shined with his glory”?

answers: Both are associated with the east
Both are associated with the north
challenge.explanation: Ezekiel is brought to the eastern gate, and the glory comes from the east and enters through it.
challenge.q: What repeated connection is made between the eastern gate and the Lord’s glory?

answers: Their whoredom and the carcases of their kings
challenge.explanation: The Lord commands them to put away their whoredom and the carcases of their kings.
challenge.q: What must Israel put away so that the Lord will dwell among them?

answers: The house is meant only for kings
God’s dwelling is connected with turning away from defilement
challenge.explanation: The passage joins the removal of defilement with the Lord’s promise to dwell among Israel forever.
challenge.q: What does the contrast between Israel’s former defilement and God’s promised dwelling teach?

paragraphs.title: Presenting the Temple’s Design and Law

easy.explanation: The Lord tells Ezekiel to show the house to the house of Israel.
easy.q: To whom was Ezekiel commanded to show the house?

easy.explanation: The purpose was that they might be ashamed of their iniquities.
easy.q: What might Israel feel when they consider what they have done?

answers: Upon the top of the mountain
easy.explanation: The law of the house says it is upon the top of the mountain.
easy.q: Where is the house described as being located?

answers: So they would keep and do them
So they could change its measurements
So they could move the house from the mountain
medium.explanation: They were to keep the whole form, ordinances, and laws of the house and do them.
medium.q: Why were the people to learn the details and laws of the house?

answers: Revelation, shame for sin, and obedience to the laws
medium.explanation: The house is shown so Israel will face its sins and keep the laws of the house.
medium.q: Which sequence best describes the purpose of showing Israel the house?

medium.explanation: The pattern refers to the design or model of the house.
medium.q: In this passage, what does the word “pattern” most nearly mean?

answers: Recognizing their sins could lead them to accept and obey the laws of the house
Recognizing their sins cancels the laws of the house
challenge.explanation: The house is shown so that shame over sin may lead to keeping its ordinances.
challenge.q: How are Israel’s recognition of sin and the presentation of the house connected?

answers: That the area has an especially high degree of holiness
That the area is intended for normal dwellings
challenge.explanation: The phrase “most holy” identifies the area as especially sacred.
challenge.q: What does “most holy” emphasize about the house and its surrounding limit?

answers: To keep and do the laws of the house
challenge.explanation: They were required not only to see the design but also to obey its ordinances and laws.
challenge.q: What was required of Israel beyond knowing the house’s design?

answers: The entrance of the Lord’s glory
easy.explanation: The verses give details about the altar’s parts and dimensions.
The KJV says, “So the altar shall be four cubits; and from the altar and upward shall be four horns.”
easy.q: How many cubits high was the altar from the altar upward, where its horns were?

easy.explanation: The verse says that the altar’s stairs looked toward the east.
easy.q: In which direction did the altar’s stairs look?

medium.explanation: The four horns are mentioned above the altar.
medium.q: What feature is described as being at the upper part of the altar?

medium.explanation: It was twelve cubits long and twelve broad, square in its four squares.
medium.q: What shape was the altar’s twelve-cubit surface?

answers: Raised projections at the altar’s corners
medium.explanation: The horns were raised parts of the altar, associated with its upper corners.
medium.q: In this passage, what are the altar’s “horns”?

challenge.explanation: The description moves from the bottom and settles upward to the altar and its horns.
challenge.q: Which order best describes the altar from its lower parts upward?

answers: Its length and width were equal, making it square
challenge.explanation: Equal length and breadth indicate a square shape.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the altar’s surface being twelve cubits long and twelve cubits broad?

answers: That the altar had no horns
That its stairs looked toward the east
That the altar was only four cubits long
challenge.explanation: The passage specifically states that its stairs looked toward the east.
challenge.q: Which detail could easily be overlooked in the description?

paragraphs.title: The Dedication of the Altar and Its Service

answers: A kid of the goats without blemish for a sin offering
easy.explanation: On the second day, a kid of the goats without blemish was offered for a sin offering.
easy.q: What was offered on the second day?

easy.explanation: The bullock was burned in the appointed place outside the sanctuary.
easy.q: Where was the bullock of the sin offering burned?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “Seven days shall they purge the altar and purify it.”
easy.q: How many days were appointed for purging and purifying the altar?

answers: On the four horns, the four corners of the settle, and the border round about
medium.explanation: The blood was placed on the horns, the corners of the settle, and the surrounding border.
medium.q: Where was the blood of the bullock to be put?

answers: A young bullock and a ram, both without blemish
medium.explanation: After the cleansing, an unblemished bullock and ram were offered.
medium.q: What was offered after the cleansing was completed?

medium.explanation: An offering without blemish was required to be sound and free from defect.
medium.q: In this context, what does “without blemish” mean?

answers: Seven days of cleansing, followed by regular offerings from the eighth day
Cleansing beginning on the eighth day, followed by seven days of offerings
Regular offerings beginning immediately on the first day
challenge.explanation: The altar was purged for seven days, and regular burnt and peace offerings began on the eighth day.
challenge.q: What is the correct sequence for the dedication of the altar?

answers: They cast salt upon the offerings before presenting them
They used salt to measure the altar
They burned the salt instead of the bullock
challenge.explanation: The priests cast salt upon the bullock and ram and then offered them as burnt offerings.
challenge.q: What was the priests’ action with the salt?

answers: After the appointed days, the Lord would accept Israel’s offerings
The dedication prevented all future offerings
The dedication was only for measuring the altar
challenge.explanation: After the eighth day, the priests would offer sacrifices, and the Lord said, “I will accept you.”
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between the altar’s dedication and Israel’s acceptance before the Lord?
